Inughuit_boats.quote: Around the 17th century, climate change cooled the northwest areas of Greenland, which cut off the Inughuit from other Inuit and regions. ... Around this period, the Inughuit also lost the knowledge to build kayaks or umiaks
Inughuit_boats.quote3: During the mid-19th century, Inuit from Baffin ... reintroduced some technologies lost to the Inughuit such as boats, leisters, and bows and arrows

Inughuit_bows_leisters.note: lost before reintroduction in mid-19th century; loss date not given

Tonga_pottery.quote3: By 1550 BP (400 AD), they ceased to produce any pottery at all.
Tonga_pottery.quote4: Speculations ... coconut cups ... underground ovens ... unsuitability of Tongan clays
Tonga_pottery.cause: demand substitution / raw material (not population collapse)

EasterIsland_seaworthy_vessels.quote: a 2007 study provided compelling evidence suggesting their arrival was closer to 1200
EasterIsland_seaworthy_vessels.quote2: Loss of large trees meant that residents were no longer able to build seaworthy vessels
EasterIsland_seaworthy_vessels.quote3: disappearance of the island's trees seems to coincide with a decline ... around the 17th and 18th centuries

Andaman_fire_making.quote: The Andamanese knew of no method for making fire in the nineteenth century.
Andaman_fire_making.note: not known whether ever had it; undated; sensitivity only

persistence_cases_descriptive.Inughuit_sleds: taught the Baffin Inuit a more advanced form of sled technology (Inughuit page)
persistence_cases_descriptive.Sentinelese_canoes: five in two canoes (Sentinelese page); isolation thousands of years (Andamanese page)
